title: Microsoft Entra ID: identity-verified account recovery for users who lose all sign-in methods (Android, iOS, desktop)
summary: Hold: the rollout checklist asks administrators to test replacement-method registration before switching the profile to Production, but Evaluation mode cannot recover an account. The licensing, default state and documented APIs are supported; three UI routes stop short of their controls.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Account recovery restores access after total loss of registered methods through third-party identity verification.
claims.quote: account recovery re-establishes trust in a user's identity through third-party identity verification before restoring access.

claims.claim: Self-service password reset requires at least one surviving authentication method.
claims.quote: Unlike self-service password reset (SSPR), which requires users to retain at least one authentication method

claims.claim: Recovery starts when the user identifies their account at sign-in and indicates they cannot access it.
claims.quote: The user provides their account identifier at sign-in and indicates they can't access their account.

claims.claim: The user is redirected to the identity verification provider specified in their profile.
claims.quote: The user is redirected to the identity verification provider specified in their applicable profile.

claims.claim: Successful verification produces a Verified ID credential stored in Microsoft Authenticator.
claims.quote: Upon successful verification, the user receives a verifiable credential (Verified ID) stored in Microsoft Authenticator.

claims.claim: The user presents that Verified ID to Entra ID.
claims.quote: The user presents their newly acquired Verified ID to Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.claim: Account validation uses directory claim mappings, a custom authentication extension, or both.
claims.quote: Account validation then uses the profile's configured directory claim mappings, a custom authentication extension, or both.

claims.claim: TAP issuance is on by default but does not enable the recovery policy.
claims.quote: TAP issuance is on by default for new and existing tenants. This default controls the registration path when recovery is enabled; it doesn't enable the tenant's Account recovery policy.

claims.claim: A recovered user can receive a TAP and register replacement methods such as passkeys without help-desk verification.
claims.quote: By default, the user receives a Temporary Access Pass (TAP) with limited validity and is guided through registering new authentication methods, such as passkeys.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; Scope; controls[0].note; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The policy is disabled for new and existing tenants until an administrator enables it, supporting admin-opt-in.
claims.quote: In the new Account recovery policy experience, the policy is disabled by default for both new and existing tenants. Enable the policy before users can use account recovery.

claims.where: Scope; controls[0].note; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Earlier preview tenants must enable the new policy; existing profiles do not enable it.
claims.quote: If your tenant already uses account recovery from an earlier preview, you also need to enable the new policy to continue using the feature. Existing identity verification profiles alone don't enable the new policy.

claims.claim: Learn labels the Account recovery settings blade as preview.
claims.quote: Open **Settings (preview)**.

claims.claim: Turning off TAP issuance is an explicit preview option.
claims.quote: **Issue Temporary Access Pass** off | Explicit preview opt-in.

claims.claim: Stale-credential cleanup is a preview control.
claims.quote: **Stale credential cleanup** is off by default and requires explicit opt-in during preview.

claims.claim: The profile preview requires the public cloud and is unavailable in national or sovereign clouds.
claims.quote: A tenant in the Microsoft public cloud. This preview isn't available in national or sovereign clouds.

claims.claim: Third-party identity verification processes government-issued documents and biometric data.
claims.quote: Identity verification involves processing government-issued documents and biometric data through third-party providers.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Providers have their own privacy and retention policies in their Security Store offers.
claims.quote: Identity verification providers have their own privacy and data retention policies as part of the verification offer from the Microsoft Security Store.

claims.claim: A custom authentication extension is optional.
claims.quote: **Custom authentication extensions** — Optional Azure Function, Logic App, or REST API endpoints that add organization-specific account validation logic during recovery.

claims.claim: Extension-processed data stays within the organisation's trust boundary.
claims.quote: Data processed by the custom authentication extension stays within the organization's trust boundary.

claims.claim: Only the extension's match result is returned to the recovery flow.
claims.quote: No organizational data is shared with Microsoft — only the match result is returned to the account recovery flow.

claims.claim: Learn warns that name-only matching may be insufficient for high-risk accounts and suggests an extension for sensitive populations.
claims.quote: For sensitive user populations, consider enabling a custom authentication extension to validate additional claims beyond first and last name. Name-only matching may not provide sufficient assurance for high-risk accounts.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Conditional Access applies to the recovery journey.
claims.quote: Yes. Conditional Access can add an extra layer of security during account recovery.

claims.claim: Terms of use, Require authentication strength and most other Entra-specific controls are unsupported for recovery and may block it or leave requirements unenforced.
claims.quote: **Terms of use**, **Require authentication strength**, and most other Microsoft Entra-specific controls aren't supported for the onboarding and recovery user action. Unsupported recovery policy requirements can block recovery or leave intended requirements unenforced.

claims.claim: With TAP issuance off and cleanup enabled, previously registered methods are deleted after recovery and replacement-passkey registration.
claims.quote: Cleanup is available only when TAP issuance is off. When cleanup is enabled, it deletes all previously registered authentication methods after both recovery and registration of the replacement passkey succeed.

claims.claim: Account recovery does not support B2B users.
claims.quote: Account recovery doesn't support B2B users, external guest users, or federated users.

claims.claim: Account recovery does not support external guest users.
claims.quote: Account recovery doesn't support B2B users, external guest users, or federated users.

claims.claim: Account recovery does not support federated users.
claims.quote: Account recovery doesn't support B2B users, external guest users, or federated users.

claims.claim: Production mode allows verified users to fully recover their accounts and receive a TAP by default.
claims.quote: **Production** — Users who complete identity verification can fully recover their accounts, receive a Temporary Access Pass by default, and re-enroll authentication methods.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Evaluation mode tests verification without recovering accounts.
claims.quote: **Evaluation** — Users can test the identity verification flow to confirm it works correctly. Accounts are **not** recovered in this mode.

claims.claim: Learn suggests human-in-the-loop recovery for sensitive accounts such as CEO or finance controller accounts.
claims.quote: For certain accounts — such as those belonging to a CEO or finance controller — you might restrict recovery to in-person or remote processes that include a human in the loop.

claims.claim: Creating a profile in the portal enables Verified ID as an authentication method for all users.
claims.quote: Creating a profile also turns on Verified ID as an authentication method for all users.

claims.claim: Profile changes can take 5-10 minutes to apply.
claims.quote: Changes to identity verification profiles can take 5-10 minutes to apply.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: The FAQ does not establish a complete TAP-free device support matrix beyond its documented limitations.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Entra account recovery TAP-free device support matrix partial deletion stale credential cleanup retries. Opened the FAQ and configuration guide; FAQ says the attestation limitation doesn't establish a complete device support matrix for other configurations.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Successful identity verification alone does not establish completed recovery or replacement-method registration.
claims.quote: Confirm that replacement-method registration completes. Successful identity verification alone doesn't establish that recovery is complete.

claims.claim: TAP issuance and cleanup are under Entra ID > Account recovery > Settings (preview) > Actions after recovery.
claims.quote: Use **Actions after recovery** in Account recovery settings to choose how users register replacement methods. **Issue Temporary Access Pass**; **Stale credential cleanup**.
claims.fix: Keep the route and add to controls[1].note: 'Under Actions after recovery, use Issue Temporary Access Pass for TAP issuance and Stale credential cleanup for cleanup.' The route currently ends at their containing section.

claims.claim: APIs for recovery-specific TAP issuance and stale-credential cleanup settings are not yet documented.

claims.claim: Recovery profiles are configured through Verified ID > ID verification profiles > Profiles.

Select Create profile, then select Recovery as Profile purpose; the wizard configures mode, user groups, provider and account validation.' These steps are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/verified-id/how-to-create-id-verification-profile.

claims.claim: verifiedIdUsageConfigurations sets the profile purpose to recovery, onboarding or all.
claims.quote: verifiedIdUsageConfigurations | Collection defining the usage purpose for the profile. The possible values are: `recovery`, `onboarding`, `all`, `unknownFutureValue`. Required.

claims.claim: The global exclusion is at Entra ID > Conditional Access > Settings (Preview) > Global exclusions > Account onboarding and recovery (Preview).
claims.quote: Browse to **Entra ID** > **Conditional Access** > **Settings (Preview)**. Under **Global exclusions**, enable the **Account onboarding and recovery (Preview)** exclusion.

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/identity/conditionalAccess/settings updates the tenant's Conditional Access global exclusion settings.
claims.quote:
Update the tenant's Conditional Access settings.
PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/identity/conditionalAccess/settings

claims.claim: The exclusion request uses exclusions.allResourcesExclusions.userActionExclusions with userAction accountrecovery.
claims.quote: "exclusions": { "allResourcesExclusions": { "userActionExclusions": [ { "state": "enabled", "userAction": "accountrecovery" } ] } }

claims.claim: The user-action exclusion supports state enabled or disabled.
claims.quote:
The **state** property supports the following values.
| enabled | The exclusion is enabled. |
| disabled | The exclusion is disabled. |
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/useractionexclusion?view=graph-rest-beta to sources; it documents the enabled and disabled exclusion states.

claims.claim: Updating userActionExclusions requires the complete desired collection.
claims.quote: When updating **userActionExclusions**, supply the complete desired collection, not only the entries that changed.

claims.claim: The Conditional Access settings API is beta and unsupported for production applications.
claims.quote: APIs under the `/beta` version in Microsoft Graph are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: A policy targeting Account onboarding and recovery is configured separately from the ID verification profile.
claims.quote: A shared profile and a Conditional Access policy are separate configuration tasks. Configure policies targeting the **Account onboarding and recovery** user action separately from the profile.

claims.where: controls[3].governs; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: The global exclusion affects all All resources policies, removing recovery from their scope when enabled.
claims.quote: Enabling the exclusion removes the **Account onboarding and recovery** user action from **All resources** policies; policies that directly target the user action still apply.

claims.claim: Partial-deletion behaviour, retries and support actions after cleanup failure still need confirmation.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Entra account recovery TAP-free device support matrix partial deletion stale credential cleanup retries. Opened FAQ and configuration guide; FAQ states: 'Partial-deletion behavior, retries, and required support actions still need confirmation.'

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout, replacement-method test
claims.claim: The Evaluation-mode pilot can be tested through replacement-method registration before the profile moves to Production.
claims.quote: **Evaluation** tests verification without recovering the account; use **Production** only for a deliberate end-to-end recovery test.
claims.fix: Replace 'Test through to replacement-method registration on the intended devices before moving the profile to Production' with 'After testing verification in Evaluation mode, use Production only for a deliberate end-to-end recovery test with the small test group; confirm replacement-method registration on the intended devices before expanding scope.' See https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/authentication/how-to-account-recovery-enable#test-recovery-settings.
